title: Insurance Housing & Corporate Rental Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Field worksheets for landing insurance relocation placements, reading the payer's ALE rules, building corporate housing demand before signing leases, and pitching landlords for rental arbitrage that survives scaling

worksheets.title: Insurance Relocation Booking and Claim Pricing Plan
worksheets.purpose: Build the property profile, portal presence, specialist outreach, and pricing math that make your home the adjuster's first pick for a displaced family, while protecting your cash flow with utility caps, family-friendly fees, a hybrid calendar, and reserves sized for unpredictable claim timing.
instructions: Complete the property profile first, because every later answer about pricing, fees, and outreach depends on the exact home you are offering to displaced families.
Submit to every relocation database you list here, then phone each one within a week to confirm receipt, since forms often send no confirmation at all.
Run the hotel comparison and Coverage D math side by side so your quote sits below the insurer's current spend and inside the family's loss-of-use budget.
Write utility caps, breakage terms, and fee amounts into the agreement and contract notes before any family signs, never after the first bill arrives.
Finish with the reserve and exit plan, and do not arbitrage a home for claims until that cash is set aside in a separate account.

fields.name: target_family_home_profile
fields.prompt: Describe the exact home you will offer displaced families: bedroom and bathroom count, pet policy, neighborhood safety, finish level, and whether the family can tour before signing. Explain why this profile beats a hotel stay and how it supports a company guarantor arrangement.
fields.example: Three-bedroom, two-bath pet-friendly house in a safe neighborhood, designer-grade finishes, open to a family walkthrough before any agreement. Bailey Kramer names the standard directly: three bedrooms, two bathrooms is best [Bailey Kramer — J-7ks576i8Q @ 00:04:22]. Jesse Vasquez warns that landing the relocator is easy while getting the family to choose your home is hard [Jesse Vasquez — O1Wmu9p-zdc @ 00:02:33].

fields.name: portal_listing_log
fields.prompt: List every relocation database you will submit to, including ALE Solutions, CRS, Sedgwick, and the Temporary Housing Directory, with submission date, listed price, and the date you will phone to confirm receipt. Note any duplicate entries discovered during follow-up calls.
fields.example: ALE Solutions form submitted Monday with a realistic monthly figure, THD form submitted the same day, confirmation calls scheduled for the following Friday. The Bougie Baldie notes the form gives no confirmation and can create duplicate entries [The Bougie Baldie — PaAH8z8rPe8 @ 00:03:13]. Bailey Kramer adds that the listed price is not the price you charge [Bailey Kramer — DFn2vbuykUY @ 00:01:17].

fields.name: specialist_email_blast
fields.prompt: Draft the weekly or biweekly email you will send to relocation specialists. Include the property headline, availability window, pet policy, and the PS and PPS lines that ask for forwards and offer referrals in other cities, so your contact list compounds each week.
fields.example: Subject: Pet-friendly 3/2 available now, family-ready. Body lists photos, move-in date, and pet terms. PS: please forward this to any specialist on your team. PPS: I can refer trusted homes in other cities. Bailey Kramer uses exactly this pairing so ten contacts become twenty the next week [Bailey Kramer — J-7ks576i8Q @ 00:09:59].

fields.name: per_night_anchor_script
fields.prompt: Write the exact words you will use on a placement call to ask for the nightly price range instead of the budget. Describe how you will stay silent until the agency names a number and how you will respond.
fields.example: Script: 'What price range per night are you working with for this family?' Then pause and let them answer. Dr Chau Ong teaches asking for the range, never the budget, because whoever gives the number first wins [Dr Chau Ong — Bbit4NDO_Hc @ 00:03:44]. Jorge Garcia cites pre-approved budgets of $8,000 to $18,000 monthly [Jorge Garcia | Roadmap Lodging — PJdlrM6k8ks @ 00:03:33].

fields.name: hotel_comparison_math
fields.prompt: Calculate what the displaced family currently costs the insurer in hotel rooms and kennel fees per month. Set your monthly quote beside that figure and state the savings you will present to the adjuster as the reason to approve.
fields.example: A family of seven in two Holiday Inn Express rooms ran about $15,000 a month; Jesse Vasquez quoted $8,100 for a house and it was accepted [Jesse Vasquez — Ncr7TdF1G34 @ 00:04:12]. Rich Somers frames $180-200 a night plus an $80 kennel as roughly $17-18K for 30 days [Rich Somers — g075AOuQIwk @ 00:28:22].

fields.name: coverage_d_budget_calc
fields.prompt: Estimate the Coverage D loss-of-use budget for your target home type. Start with purchase price, strip out land value, apply the 20-30% dwelling percentage, and divide across six and twelve months to find a defensible monthly quote.
fields.example: On a $480K Smyrna purchase, Ruben Kanya strips roughly 10% land using a cost segregation study, leaving $432K dwelling. At 20% that is $86,400, or $7,200 a month over 12 months and $14,400 over six [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — vbHlGVZKjvg @ 00:45:27]. That range sets the ceiling for the quote.

fields.name: utility_cap_terms
fields.prompt: Write the electric and water cap language you will place in the agreement and contract notes before signing. State the monthly threshold, who pays above it, and how you will document readings so overages are billed cleanly.
fields.example: Contract note: guest pays all electric above $500 per month and water above a stated cap, billed from the monthly statement. Jesse Vasquez learned this the hard way when uncapped electric ran about $1,000 a month on the $8,100 house, and now writes caps in up front [Jesse Vasquez — O1Wmu9p-zdc @ 00:06:27].

fields.name: fee_schedule_review
fields.prompt: List your cleaning, pet, and deposit fees and compare them with competing homes. Explain how each fee lands on a family paying out of pocket and which fees you will reduce so the total does not cost you the booking.
fields.example: Cleaning $150, pet $75, deposit $200, total $425 versus a competitor near $1,000. Bailey Kramer reminds operators that the families are the ones who have to pay the fees [Bailey Kramer — J-7ks576i8Q @ 00:19:33], and a $1,000 versus $200 gap loses bookings [Bailey Kramer — J-7ks576i8Q @ 00:19:46]. Lower fees keep the family choosing you.

fields.name: hybrid_calendar_rules
fields.prompt: Define how you will run a duplicate 30-day-minimum Airbnb listing beside your agency listings. State the maximum short-stay booking window, which holiday weekends you will refuse in advance, and how long you will hold a unit pending adjuster approval.
fields.example: STR window open no more than 30 days out, and no Fourth of July bookings accepted in May [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — vbHlGVZKjvg @ 00:35:03]. Treat ASAP as at least a week, and hold the unit 24 hours pending adjuster approval rather than releasing it [She's Got Assets — 5Py6jcyyUyA @ 01:19:18].

fields.name: reserve_and_exit_plan
fields.prompt: Record the cash reserve you will hold before arbitraging a home for claims, the months it covers, and three exit strategies if claim leads dry up. Name the trigger date for activating each exit and who approves it.
fields.example: Reserve of six months of all-in cost, about $19,800 on a $3,300 monthly run rate. Exits: midterm nurse lease, standard furnished monthly, long-term tenant. Jose Luiz Morales requires at least six months of reserves and three exit strategies before arbitraging a home for claims [Jose Luiz Morales — 5tg19JIMU0o @ 00:35:50].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not accept an insurance placement until every portal submission is phone-confirmed, electric and water caps are written into the agreement and notes, total family-paid fees sit near the low end of local competitors, and at least six months of reserves plus three exit strategies are documented.

worksheets.title: Payer-Side Intake and Corporate Housing Demand Builder
worksheets.purpose: Learn to read a claim the way the adjuster does, confirming habitability, ALE limits, runway, and comparable pricing, then convert that understanding into a corporate housing operation built demand-first, underwritten at conservative occupancy, and protected by direct client relationships and verified guests.
instructions: Confirm the uninhabitable finding and the shape of the ALE limit before quoting, because ALE only pays the increase over normal living costs on a covered loss.
Price against comparable local housing the carrier would accept, not against the highest number you hope to collect, since agencies negotiate rates down.
Ask about pets, trips, and breakage on the first call so disputes never surface on the back end of the stay.
Lock at least one relocation, adjuster, or HR relationship before you sign, furnish, or list any corporate housing unit.
Underwrite at 80% occupancy and verify every employer and occupant before handing over keys.

fields.name: habitability_trigger_check
fields.prompt: Record how you will confirm the family's home was deemed uninhabitable by authorities or the adjuster after a covered loss. Note which document or phone confirmation you will request before quoting, and who on the claim provides it.
fields.example: Before quoting, ask the relocation specialist to confirm the adjuster has deemed the home uninhabitable and opened ALE. Be A Claims Adjuster states the home must be deemed uninhabitable by the authorities or by the insurance company's adjuster [Be A Claims Adjuster — _Odm8IhYr80 @ 00:01:46]. No uninhabitable finding, no ALE money, no booking.

fields.name: ale_limit_runway
fields.prompt: Document whether the family's ALE limit is a dollar cap, a time cap, both, or neither, and estimate how much runway remains. Explain how that runway sets your contract length and the extension you will offer.
fields.example: Policy written at 30% of a $300,000 dwelling gives a $90,000 cap [Insurance Savvy — Xnrpk3PKFg4 @ 00:02:33]; an Actual Loss Sustained policy usually runs up to 12 months [Crowley Insurance Agency, Inc — TkI2Qak3r34 @ 00:01:15]. United Policyholders warns a neighbor's policy can read completely differently [United Policyholders — bPQqrGrXfiI @ 00:05:54].

fields.name: california_duration_note
fields.prompt: If the claim falls under California rules, record the 24-month floor, the possible extension to 36 months, and the construction delays that justify it. Note how you will align your lease term with that longer timeline.
fields.example: California sets a 24-month ALE minimum, extendable up to 36 months in 6-month increments for good-faith permit, materials or contractor delays, but the extension is not automatic [United Policyholders — bPQqrGrXfiI @ 00:22:58]. Offer a renewable term with a 30-day check-in tied to the family's rebuild schedule so your calendar is never surprised.

fields.name: comparable_pricing
fields.prompt: Identify comparable local housing the carrier would consider equivalent to the family's prior home, and set your monthly price against it. Explain why a quote far above the comparable will be cut back by the adjuster or agency.
fields.example: Kela Trishaan prices a San Diego 3bd/2ba at about $5,000 a month and notes the carrier does not owe for a $10,000 place [Kela Trishaan — awTD63In04A @ 00:06:59]. Jesse Vasquez adds that agencies negotiate lower rates so they don't use up the policyholder's ALE [Jesse Vasquez — 70ZSuGbTIJo @ 00:04:54].

fields.name: intake_pets_and_trips
fields.prompt: List the intake questions you will ask the family or specialist on the first call, covering pets, pre-planned trips, household size, and move-in date. Explain why raising each item at the start prevents disputes later in the stay.
fields.example: Intake script: How many people and pets? Any trips planned during the claim? Target move-in date? Kela Trishaan says it is better to have the conversation in the beginning than argue on the back end [Kela Trishaan — awTD63In04A @ 00:13:11], citing a pre-planned birthday trip denied mid-claim [Kela Trishaan — awTD63In04A @ 00:13:23].

fields.name: breakage_responsibility
fields.prompt: Write the breakage clause for insurance families: who pays for damaged furniture, appliances, and small items, how damage is documented at move-in and move-out, and how you will explain it to the family before they sign.
fields.example: Clause: normal wear covered by the owner; breakage beyond wear billed to the household with photos from the turnover inspection. Driven Saver describes families paying for a refrigerator and even a thrown-away fork [Driven Saver — uCQYAZ1ws_w @ 00:04:31], so spell it out up front instead of surprising a family already in crisis.

fields.name: demand_first_relationship
fields.prompt: Name at least one relocation manager, adjuster, or HR contact you will lock in before signing any lease. Record how you met them, what housing they need, and the next date you will follow up with them.
fields.example: Contact: regional HR lead met through BNI, needs two furnished units for crews on 90-day rotations. Jorge Garcia locks demand before any lease because demand first eliminates 90% of the risk [Jorge Garcia | Roadmap Lodging — Ewazlh6zOLM @ 00:01:21]. Jesse Vasquez adds that direct relationships insulate you from industry shifts [Jesse Vasquez — 70ZSuGbTIJo @ 00:09:39].

fields.name: three_edges_location
fields.prompt: Score your target unit against the three-edges location rule of hospitals, highways, and hotels, plus Wi-Fi, blackout curtains, a desk, and a full kitchen. Note any gap you must fix before pitching corporate clients and estimate what each fix will cost.
fields.example: Unit sits near a hospital, two minutes from the highway, and close to a hotel row where work trucks park. Jesse Vasquez photographs trucks at Extended Stay America and Holiday Inn Express, then pitches those companies on savings versus hotel spend [Jesse Vasquez — ypZmx1qTnpY @ 00:02:47]. Gap: add blackout curtains and a desk.

fields.name: occupancy_underwriting
fields.prompt: Underwrite the unit at 80% occupancy and show monthly revenue, rent, and net at that level. Compare against the 95% mature-operator benchmark and state whether the deal still works if occupancy falls short of your target.
fields.example: Avenue West will not bring a property into its program unless it can rent it more than 80% of the time [RPOAM Real Estate Investor Podcast — f2vS4cnBnoI @ 00:14:33]. Gabriel Wacker runs about 95% occupied [Vivian Yip — DNkNK6FNKog @ 00:20:45]. Model both levels before signing the lease.

fields.name: guest_verification_and_billing
fields.prompt: Describe how you will verify the employer, background-check every occupant for evictions and fraud, and set up payment. Note how you will keep the client relationship direct rather than letting an online travel agency control cancellations and fees.
fields.example: LaShaun Shanae verifies the employer, background-checks every occupant for evictions and fraud, and has the employer pay by credit card [LaShaun Shanae — nZd4KYLOZDw @ 00:14:56]. PBD Living warns that OTAs take a cut and control cancellations, so build direct booking with LinkedIn and Facebook ads to adjusters and HR [PBD Living | Furnished Housing — DviX_t2s-0E @ 00:03:58].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign a corporate or insurance housing lease until the uninhabitable finding and ALE limit type are confirmed, your price sits at the local comparable, intake questions on pets and trips are logged, one named demand relationship is locked, and the unit pencils at 80% occupancy.

worksheets.title: Landlord Pitch, Lease Terms, and Scaling Stress Test
worksheets.purpose: Turn landlord outreach into signed leases by pitching as a corporate housing company, answering rent and condition fears with proof, and negotiating terms that protect capital, then stress-test every unit against a minimum net, an automation stack, concentration risk, insurance, and local ordinances before scaling.
instructions: Never lead with Airbnb; write every script and tour talking point around a corporate housing company placing professionals in furnished units.
Set your maximum rent before the first call so a persuasive landlord cannot talk you into a spread that never pays back.
Log every rejection with its reason, because repeated objections show you exactly where your script needs to change.
Prove unit one profitable at your minimum net before you add unit two, and have your automation stack running the day the lease is signed.
Bind your own insurance and read local ordinances repeatedly before committing capital to any additional unit or market.

fields.name: corporate_housing_opener
fields.prompt: Write the opening line you will use when calling or touring with a landlord, framing your business as a corporate housing company. Include the filter question you will ask about short-term furnished leases and how you will follow up.
fields.example: Opener: We are a corporate housing company placing professionals in furnished units. Do you allow leases for short-term furnished housing? Aurelio Licata's lesson six is don't say Airbnb, say corporate housing company [Aurelio Licata — Q3hSpjquUTE @ 00:06:28], and Rafa Loza uses the filter question because it opens a conversation [Rafa Loza — 894g1JF-IuM @ 00:13:25].

fields.name: landlord_fear_answers
fields.prompt: List the two landlord fears, on-time rent and property condition, and write your answer to each. Include the payment proof you will show, the damage responsibility language, and the cleaning frequency you will commit to in writing.
fields.example: Rent: autopay set two days early, and when asked how they know you'll pay, show the autopay confirmation itself [Jorge Contreras | Airbnb Arbitrage — _M0OdXelhoU @ 00:03:55]. Jorge Contreras sets up the property on autopay two days early [Jorge Contreras | Airbnb Arbitrage — d8qhoiAWdLs @ 00:01:43]. Condition: written damage responsibility plus frequent professional cleaning.

fields.name: rent_cap_and_spread
fields.prompt: Set the maximum rent you will accept for this unit based on projected revenue. Show the rent-to-revenue spread, the nightly rate relative to monthly rent, and the asking price at which you will walk away from the deal, even after negotiation.
fields.example: Sean Rakidzich pays $2,000 and charges $3,000, with one guideline: don't pay too much in rent [Sean Rakidzich — lGwvDjwR4uU @ 00:05:05]. Linda Kim walked from a $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need [Linda Kim — 5vV0oy-jJ7g @ 00:31:38]. Ceiling here: $1,900 rent against a $3,000 projection, before any concession.

fields.name: lease_terms_and_free_rent
fields.prompt: Outline the lease terms you will request: length, LLC signer, start-date gap after signing, free-rent concession, and escape clause. Explain how each term protects your capital during setup and if the market or building changes. Note which term you will trade away first.
fields.example: Request a two-to-three-year lease in the LLC's name, signed June 1 and beginning June 15 [Jorge Contreras | Airbnb Arbitrage — _M0OdXelhoU @ 00:05:06]. Colin Wright gets free rent on all deals because Wright won't take deals without it [Official Success Formula — NSyEBVGX02o @ 00:58:03], plus a one-to-two-month escape clause.

fields.name: startup_capital_plan
fields.prompt: Total your startup capital for unit one: first month, deposit, furniture, photos, and setup. Identify how you will fund it without a business loan and how many months of revenue you need to recover it at your projected net.
fields.example: Rafa Loza puts per-unit setup at $5,000-$15,000 depending on market and started with $6K cash plus a $9K credit card for furniture [Rafa Loza — 894g1JF-IuM @ 00:06:40]. LoCasa warns that if unit one isn't profitable, more units won't solve it [LoCasa — OSi_ARPIpaM @ 00:00:42]. Plan: $11,000 total, recovered in six months.

fields.name: rejection_quota_log
fields.prompt: Set your daily outreach quota for landlord and apartment-complex calls, and log each rejection with the reason given. Note which objections repeat so you can adjust your script before the next round of calls. Also list buildings under construction you will target.
fields.example: Quota: at least one call a day, logged by building and objection. Rafa Loza heard 30+ no's before the first yes and 20+ more before the second [Joshua Baldovino — 1JRlBob3GhE @ 00:20:58]. Target new construction too, since those owners have vacancy to solve for years to come [Joshua Baldovino — 1JRlBob3GhE @ 00:47:46].

fields.name: minimum_net_threshold
fields.prompt: State the minimum monthly net each property must produce to stay in your portfolio. Show the projected net for this unit and decide whether to keep, renegotiate, or walk away, along with the date you will review it.
fields.example: Richie Matthews: if you're not spitting out at least $2,000 to $2,500 per month per property, walk away from the deal or better yet, negotiate it [Richie Matthews — VtVf0h80q0w @ 00:06:44]. This unit projects $1,600 net, so renegotiate rent down $500 or exit before the escape window closes.

fields.name: automation_and_va_stack
fields.prompt: List the software and virtual assistant setup you will have running the day the lease is signed: messaging, calendar sync, dynamic pricing, and written protocols. Note the monthly cost and which tasks you will delegate first.
fields.example: Stack: Hospitable at $40 plus dynamic pricing at $40, about $80 a month [Richie Matthews — O4cBKKUBS64 @ 00:13:29]. Delegate guest messaging and cleaner scheduling to a VA first. Matthews went from 18 to 35 units in six months after delegating [Richie Matthews — VtVf0h80q0w @ 00:04:01], because you can't scale chaos.

fields.name: unit_concentration_check
fields.prompt: Map where your current and planned units sit and flag any building or block where you are stacking more than one. Explain whether local demand can absorb the stacked units without cannibalizing your own bookings and rates.
fields.example: Humza Zafar warns against stacking units in one building or across the street outside Dubai or New York-type demand; Detroit cannibalization cost about $100K [Humza Zafar — 1D3J3ID1ZZM @ 00:53:42]. Current plan: two units in one mid-size building, third unit moved to a separate neighborhood to protect rates.

fields.name: coverage_and_regulation_check
fields.prompt: Record the traditional insurance you will bind after signing, including liability and loss of income, and summarize the local ordinances you have read. Note any city-staff answers you still need to verify before committing more capital.
fields.example: Bind traditional coverage with liability and loss of income for a 3-4 month repair instead of relying on the Airbnb host guarantee [Short Term Sage - Airbnb, Vacation Rental Host — wt5AlXFsjDQ @ 00:19:07]. Read the ordinances repeatedly and take city-staff answers with a grain of salt [Joshua Baldovino — 1JRlBob3GhE @ 00:46:39].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign a second arbitrage lease until unit one clears your minimum monthly net, the lease includes a start-date gap and escape clause under your LLC, your automation stack and VA protocols are live, no building is overstacked, and your own liability and loss-of-income coverage is bound.

worksheets.title: Midterm Rental Setup and the Airbnb Pivot Math
worksheets.purpose: Turn the midterm rental fundamentals and pivot economics into a launch file for one door: furnishing budget, rent multiple, conservative occupancy, payment and deposit controls, listing copy, insurance confirmation, and the tax schedule decision, all built before a single lease is signed.
instructions: Work one property at a time; every figure on this sheet belongs to a single address and a single furnished unit.
Use the conservative number whenever a range appears, then note the upside figure separately so it never drives the decision.
Complete the pivot stress test at both 95% and 65% occupancy before you buy furniture or cancel any long-term lease.
Make the insurer call and the tax review before listing, because both answers can change the rent you need to charge.
Keep every citation next to the number it supports so you can defend each assumption to a partner, lender, or yourself.

fields.name: furnishing_budget
fields.prompt: Calculate the furnishing budget for your unit using the per-square-foot rule. Enter the square footage, the low and high cost range, whether you will handle assembly yourself, and the month by which furniture must pay itself back from rent.
fields.example: 1,000 sq ft three-bedroom: $10,000 low, $15,000 high, because the rule of thumb runs 10 to 15 dollars per square foot including assembly labor [Bailey Kramer — De_DgYIghMo @ 00:03:12]. I will assemble myself to pull toward the low end. Payback target: month 10, matching the $6,000-furnishing illustration paid back in a little over 10 months [John Racine — iNwc9csMvTA @ 00:09:08].

fields.name: rent_multiple_target
fields.prompt: Set the monthly base rent for the furnished unit by applying a multiple to the local long-term rent. Record the long-term comp, the multiple you chose, the resulting monthly rent, and the deposit you will collect as a fraction of a month.
fields.example: Long-term comp $2,000. Multiple 1.5x to 2x, the base-rent rule of thumb from a Furnished Finder marketing director who owns 13 MTRs [Furnished Finder — JG03P3JsuHc @ 00:25:43]. Target rent $3,000 to $4,000. Deposit set at one-third to one-half of a month, so $1,000 to $2,000. Floor check: single-family comps run 35% above long-term [Midterm Rental Consulting — GC5LW4scQwo @ 00:00:55].

fields.name: occupancy_underwriting
fields.prompt: Underwrite the unit at a conservative occupancy rather than the best-case figure you hope for. Write the occupancy percentage you will model, the number of vacant months you expect per year, and the cash reserve you will hold before launch.
fields.example: Modeled occupancy 80 to 85%, with about two vacant months a year and a three-month cash reserve in place before the first guest [Real Life Planning with Cynthia Meyer — icpm0fFsk6Y @ 00:07:54]. Upside reference only: one operator reports 92% occupancy with under one week vacant between rentals [Midterm Rental Consulting — GC5LW4scQwo @ 00:00:55]. Reserve amount: three months of rent plus utilities.

fields.name: payment_and_keys_policy
fields.prompt: Define the payment rule that controls when keys are released to an incoming tenant. List the automated payment channel you will use, the payment apps you will refuse, and the exact step that must clear before anyone receives access.
fields.example: No keys until first month's rent clears through the automated rent channel; Zelle, Venmo, and Cash App are refused outright [Jesse Vasquez — VtuboLMzJj0 @ 00:11:05]. The signed lease is the release trigger, because the lease is your safety net [Jesse Vasquez — VtuboLMzJj0 @ 00:04:48]. Monthly check: send somebody every single month [Jesse Vasquez — VtuboLMzJj0 @ 00:16:04].

fields.name: deposit_handling
fields.prompt: Describe where security deposits will be held and how deductions will be proven. Name the dedicated account, the documentation you will keep for each deduction, and whether you will rely on the platform damage waiver or skip it entirely.
fields.example: Deposit goes into a dedicated savings account opened for this property only, with every deduction documented, and the Furnished Finder damage waiver is skipped [Midterm Rental Consulting — PLf1d4djjZw @ 00:05:14]. Cleaners photograph the unit before each check-in and after each checkout so disputes never turn into hearsay [Jacob and Elissa — ZoPbBZvfW94 @ 00:03:34].

fields.name: lease_deadline_screening
fields.prompt: Set the deadline an approved applicant has to sign the lease and fund the deposit. Explain how you will treat applicants who miss it, and state whether your calendar stays open to other inquiries until both steps are finished.
fields.example: Applicants get 72 hours to sign and fund the deposit; anyone who ghosts the process is treated as a future bad tenant [Midterm Rental Consulting — r-8W10XEuGg @ 00:05:06]. The calendar stays open, following the rule do not block your calendar until you have a lease signed [Airbnb Hosting and Short Term Rental Tips — 264jEA_cXOw @ 00:19:55]. Backup applicants stay queued.

fields.name: listing_copy_plan
fields.prompt: Draft the opening lines of your Furnished Finder description and the photo shot list. Specify where your contact email appears, whether you write in bullets or prose, and which practical items and safety features each photo and bullet must show.
fields.example: First line: email address as a bullet, then bullets only, no flowery prose, since past wins came from direct one-to-one emails with nurses [Midterm Rental Consulting — kaZB8y5juss @ 00:00:51]. Shot list: coffee machine, dishes, Tupperware, blackout curtains, towels. Copy bullets: security, lighting, free parking [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — XTn3a_-I1Rg @ 00:04:37]. Photos stay true-to-property.

fields.name: pivot_stress_test
fields.prompt: Run the STR-to-MTR pivot math before switching any door. Enter the current long-term comp, projected monthly furnished rent, added utilities and cleaning costs, and the resulting net at both a strong and a weak occupancy scenario.
fields.example: Scenario from a $3,000-comp illustration: $4,800 of added costs leaves a net gain of only about $1,800, which is exactly why you have to run the numbers [John Racine — iNwc9csMvTA @ 00:08:21]. Stress test at 95% and at 65% occupancy, with added utilities and cleaning counted before calling it a raise [John Racine — iNwc9csMvTA @ 00:12:36].

fields.name: insurance_call_script
fields.prompt: Script the call to your insurer before the first monthly guest arrives. Record the exact phrase you will use to describe the operation, the coverage question you will ask, and what the renter's own policy does and does not protect.
fields.example: Opening line: this is a furnished mid-term rental. Question: does the landlord package allow furnished short-to-mid occupancy, or does it assume a 12-month lease [Short-Term Stays & Rentals — QIziS47827w @ 00:01:50]? Gap noted: a renter's policy usually covers only their belongings, not walls, appliances, or liability exposure [Short-Term Stays & Rentals — QIziS47827w @ 00:01:35].

fields.name: tax_schedule_check
fields.prompt: Determine how rental income will be reported this year. Note how many days the unit will be rented, the expected average stay length, and every guest service you provide, then mark whether the operation leans toward Schedule E or Schedule C.
fields.example: Rented well over 14 days, so the income is reportable [Lodge Compliance — zQI1CpxOnQ0 @ 00:01:32]. Average stay is monthly, far above 7 days. Services: turnover cleaning and linens only, no daily maid service, meals, airport rides, or concierge, which keeps the unit off the 15.3% Schedule C self-employment path [Restart Tax Talk — SpF7mXFixD8 @ 00:00:59]. Lean: Schedule E.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when the unit has a written furnishing budget and payback month, rent set at a stated multiple of long-term rent, underwriting at 80 to 85% occupancy with a three-month reserve, the payment and deposit rules written, insurer confirmation in hand, and the pivot net positive at 65% occupancy.

worksheets.title: Nurse and Contract-Worker Housing with Airtight Lease Paper
worksheets.purpose: Build the demand, screening, and paperwork system for 13-week travelers: confirm hospital demand, equip and list the unit for nurses, screen every adult, block payment fraud, write extension and sublease clauses, and collect the insurance certificates that keep a master lease and subtenants protected.
instructions: Start with the hospital HR call; if demand is weak, stop here before spending money on furniture or a lease.
Write every clause in plain language a tenant can read in one pass, and keep each permission in writing.
Send the sublease addendum during the opening negotiation so the owner sees every term before the signing table.
Treat the payment protocol as non-negotiable; share it with every tenant before the first dollar moves.
Archive signed addenda and certificates in a property folder so permission survives any change in management.

fields.name: hospital_demand_check
fields.prompt: Verify traveler demand before you buy or lease near a hospital. Record the hospital name, the drive time from the unit, who you reached in human resources, and what they said about traveler housing demand and typical contract length.
fields.example: Target radius: within about 20 minutes of the hospital, filled by 13-week contracts that often extend. Called hospital HR about traveler housing demand before buying; their answer beats any market report [The CoLiving Insider — VbsbBFnJvik @ 00:06:17]. Benchmark: ensuite rehabs one mile from Johns Hopkins hold 95-97% occupancy [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — utDX2blYFMk @ 00:21:36].

fields.name: nurse_amenity_checklist
fields.prompt: List every amenity a travel nurse will check before booking your unit. Mark each item as installed, ordered, or missing, and note which of them you will feature in photos and which you will call out in the listing text.
fields.example: Installed: blackout curtains, fast Wi-Fi, in-unit laundry, quality bed. Ordered: desk and full kitchen kit. Pets: dogs allowed, since flipping to pet friendly raised revenue 30% [Clint Coons Esq. | Real Estate Asset Protection — 2WVMiZV3TYI @ 00:16:39]. Listing text calls out security, lighting and free parking [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — XTn3a_-I1Rg @ 00:04:37].

fields.name: inquiry_response_standard
fields.prompt: Commit to a response standard for every inquiry from nurses and contract workers. Write the maximum reply window, who covers inquiries when you are unavailable, and the pre-recorded materials you will send instead of scheduling an in-person showing.
fields.example: Reply window: same day, every inquiry, because a nurse who does not hear back the same day books somewhere else [The CoLiving Insider — VbsbBFnJvik @ 00:05:24]. Target is minutes, not hours, with true-to-property photos and a pre-recorded walkthrough replacing in-person showings [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — n77MirHjIVo @ 00:26:26]. Backup responder: my named backup contact.

fields.name: tenant_screening_standard
fields.prompt: Set the screening standard every occupant must pass before a lease is offered. Specify which adults are screened, the checks you run on each, and whether you still verify credit when a staffing agency or employer already vetted the tenant.
fields.example: Every adult 18 and over is screened, and credit is still checked even when the employer has already vetted the nurse [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — XTn3a_-I1Rg @ 00:24:14]. For corporate placements, the employer is verified and every occupant is background-checked for evictions and fraud, with the employer paying by credit card [LaShaun Shanae — nZd4KYLOZDw @ 00:14:56].

fields.name: payment_fraud_guard
fields.prompt: Write the payment-safety protocol you will share with every tenant before money changes hands. Include when the first payment is accepted, how you test the receiving account, and the exact sentence that warns tenants about fake payment requests.
fields.example: No money is taken before the lease is signed. A $1 test payment runs into a separate bank account first, and tenants are told that I will never request money outside the agreed process [Caytlyn Cole Tolliver — ObdxpkrC-yE @ 00:10:02]. Warning sentence: I will never request money [Caytlyn Cole Tolliver — ObdxpkrC-yE @ 00:12:35]. Never Zelle, Venmo, or Cash App.

fields.name: extension_notice_clause
fields.prompt: Draft the lease clause that governs contract extensions for 13-week tenants. State the minimum notice you require, what happens to the calendar if notice is late, and how you handle the next applicant waiting in your queue meanwhile.
fields.example: Clause: tenant must give at least one month's notice of any contract extension, so the calendar can be held or released for the next tenant in the queue [Caytlyn Cole Tolliver — KIPX-8cQrqc @ 00:07:27]. Queue rule: never turn anyone away until a lease is signed and a deposit is made [Caytlyn Cole Tolliver — KIPX-8cQrqc @ 00:01:27]. Late notice releases the dates.

fields.name: room_vs_whole_unit
fields.prompt: Compare renting the unit whole against renting it by the room. Enter the whole-unit monthly rent, the per-room rent multiplied by room count, the occupancy you will underwrite for each model, and the turnover cost per room.
fields.example: Whole unit: $2,000-$2,200. By the room: 2 x $1,250 = $2,500, and about 20% of Furnished Finder listings rent by the room [Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast — XTn3a_-I1Rg @ 00:12:06]. Room model underwritten at 75% occupancy, not 100%, with $100-$150 per room turnover and more than one guest source [The CoLiving Insider — VbsbBFnJvik @ 00:05:42].

fields.name: recruiter_feeder_channel
fields.prompt: Map a direct feeder channel that sends tenants to you without competing in the listing scrum. Name the staffing agencies, recruiters, or hospital contacts you will approach, the platform you will use to find them, and your partnership pitch.
fields.example: Channel: staffing recruiters found on LinkedIn, plus direct calls to the agency pitching a housing partnership [Bailey Kramer — phifsNzsrJk @ 00:11:28]. Backup listing: Furnished Finder at $99 per listing for a 12-month membership with no booking fee, since one month-long booking pays for the year [The House Hacking Podcast — 63S3a8R7kZs @ 00:05:32]. Pitch opens with a question, not a hard sell.

fields.name: sublease_addendum_terms
fields.prompt: List every term your one-page sublease addendum must contain before the first listing goes live. Cover stay-length language, named platforms, guest types, a ban or pandemic opt-out, which document prevails, and when the addendum reaches the owner.
fields.example: Terms: under-30-day hosting permitted, platforms named, addendum prevails over the lease, and a 60-day no-penalty opt-out after a government-mandated short-term rental ban or pandemic restrictions [LoCasa — VFt0XueZxpE @ 00:07:05]. Guest types broadened to all travelers so the landlord cannot turn the tables later [LoCasa — VFt0XueZxpE @ 00:01:56]. Addendum sent during the opening negotiation, not at signing.

fields.name: liability_certificate_requirements
fields.prompt: Record the insurance proof required on both sides of the lease. Enter the liability limit on your certificate, whether the landlord is named as additional insured, the minimum liability each subtenant must carry, and the renters insurance requirement.
fields.example: Certificate: $1,000,000 per occurrence with the additional insured box checked for the landlord [Commercial Real Estate Pro Network — ZVbVs2WDmLw @ 00:03:16]. Subtenant liability minimum: $100,000. Renters insurance required on every new lease and renewal, citing the national average of about $132 a year for a $100,000 limit [BiggerPockets — 8MMoqEHoIn0 @ 00:03:49]. Coverage verified on paper, never assumed.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when hospital demand is confirmed by phone, the amenity list is fully installed, screening covers every adult with credit checked, the payment protocol and extension clause are written into the lease, the signed addendum is archived, and liability certificates are on file.

worksheets.title: Exit Clauses, Tenant Protections, and the Right Insurance Stack
worksheets.purpose: Price every way out of a lease before signing it and insure the operation so a claim actually pays: termination fees, state rules, protected exits, signed termination agreements, move-out proof, California just cause checks, the policy conversion call, liability limits, honest use disclosure, and safety items.
instructions: Read the early termination clause and notice clock before signing; the exit price is set on day one, not at move-out.
Look up your state's rules yourself and confirm them with a local landlord tenant attorney before relying on them.
Never stop paying rent or hand back keys without a signed termination agreement and a written key receipt.
Make the 15-minute insurance conversion call before any tenant, guest, or room renter moves in.
Disclose the real occupancy model in writing and update the carrier before renewal whenever rooms or guest types change.

fields.name: termination_fee_terms
fields.prompt: Price the early exit before you sign any lease, as tenant or as landlord. Record the termination fee or buyout written into the agreement, how many months of rent it equals, and how it compares with paying rent on an empty unit.
fields.example: Master lease buyout: two months rent, matching the typical landlord-side buyout of around two months [DoorLoop — DMY8aqSWFmQ @ 00:03:58]. The common range runs 1 to 3 months rent and can be cheaper than paying rent on an unoccupied unit until the lease is up [Tenant Law Group, PC — mXtFESh8Jwc @ 00:01:19]. On $2,000 rent, exit cost is $4,000.

fields.name: state_rule_lookup
fields.prompt: Look up the rules in the state where the unit sits before relying on any exit plan. Note whether the landlord has a duty to re-rent, any statutory cap on default charges, and the local attorney you contacted for direction.
fields.example: Searched landlord's duty to re-rent plus the state, then called a local landlord tenant attorney, since many give direction for free [Adulting Shouldn't Suck — 07RfH5S46pg @ 00:05:28]. Florida note: default damages capped at up to two months of rent under Florida Statutes 83.595 when the lease lacks its own default section [The Listing Real Estate Management — WU7IqO6I6fk @ 00:02:04].

fields.name: protected_exit_review
fields.prompt: Identify every exit that can release a tenant without penalty regardless of what the lease says. Note military orders, domestic violence documentation, habitability or quiet-enjoyment failures, and illegal units, plus the notice clock that applies to each one.
fields.example: Military: permanent change of station or deployment orders of 90 days or more end the lease 30 days after the next rent date, with written notice plus orders and no early termination fee [60SecondLaw — X_XeyY10oQE @ 00:03:50]. Also flagged: habitability, quiet-enjoyment, domestic violence, illegal units. Ontario rule: expiry is not a termination ground [Ontario Renter Rights — N08BrJ9_Luw @ 00:01:18].

fields.name: termination_agreement_checklist
fields.prompt: Draft the termination agreement that must exist before anyone moves out or stops paying rent. List the signatures required, the dollar amount owed, the move-out date, and the release language confirming that no further rent is due afterward.
fields.example: No move-out and no rent stoppage until both sides sign an agreement stating the amount, the move-out date, and that no further rent is owed [60SecondLaw — X_XeyY10oQE @ 00:05:52]. If no buyout exists, a written reminder of the landlord's duty to re-rent goes out citing the state statute, and every vacant week with no listing is logged [60SecondLaw — X_XeyY10oQE @ 00:06:09].

fields.name: move_out_documentation
fields.prompt: Plan the move-out documentation that protects the deposit on your way out of a master lease. Describe the cleaning and repairs completed, the photos and videos captured, how keys are returned, and what proof you keep afterward.
fields.example: Unit cleaned, repaired, and documented with my own photos and videos before vacating to block deposit deductions [Better Call Kal — 2ZipHRbP_7U @ 00:06:13]. Keys returned against a written receipt, with nothing I want and no occupants left in the apartment [The Legal Aid Society — sIjDgu8Ns9w @ 00:01:10]. Files saved in the property folder alongside the original move-in condition photos.

fields.name: just_cause_exemption_check
fields.prompt: Before starting any eviction or non-renewal in California, document the AB 1482 exemption determination. Record whether the property is exempt, the basis for that conclusion, and the just cause ground you will rely on if it is not exempt.
fields.example: Exemption determination is run before any eviction, because a non-exempt property without just cause will likely lose the case [David Piotrowski — dOXVjIvVseI @ 00:07:40]. Tenant waivers are not relied on, since just cause requirements cannot be waived even if the tenant agrees [David Piotrowski — dOXVjIvVseI @ 00:07:56]. Determination memo is filed with the lease.

fields.name: policy_conversion_call
fields.prompt: Script the conversion call that rewrites the property's coverage before a tenant or guest moves in. Record the agent's name, the exact policy form you request, the endorsements you add, and the named insured shown on the declarations.
fields.example: Fifteen-minute call before move-in telling the agent this address is becoming a rental [Real Property Management Palisade — aUKpl6xobwU @ 00:02:05]. Form: dwelling fire pushed to DP3 with replacement cost, loss of rent, vandalism, and water coverage. Named insured matches the deed, including the LLC [Bryan Gutowsky | Michigan Insurance — UUWJRIHQaqk @ 00:03:22].

fields.name: liability_limits_stack
fields.prompt: Set the liability stack that sits behind every rental door. Enter the per-property liability limit, whether an umbrella policy sits on top, how premiums compare with the old homeowner policy, and whether multiple homes can share one bundled policy.
fields.example: Liability: at least $500,000 per door [Blue Fox Properties — 7sscnFcWkp4 @ 00:03:58], stacked toward $1 million with an umbrella on top. Premium expectation: about 25 percent more than homeowner coverage for the same property [Steadily — 8qVhmrP1DZM @ 00:01:22]. Scaling plan: up to 30 homes on one bill with one renewal date [AmericanModernIns — fR49bewBEuo @ 00:00:44].

fields.name: use_disclosure
fields.prompt: Write the exact use disclosure you will give your carrier in writing. Describe the occupancy model, the number of rooms and agreements, the guest types, and the date you will report any change in rooms or guest mix before renewal.
fields.example: Disclosure: rent-by-the-room to unrelated adults on separate agreements, with every change in rooms or guest type reported before renewal [The CoLiving Insider — RyLyOzBiWEs @ 00:10:10]. Reason: a six-unit, roughly 3,000 sq ft room house described as a 1,600 sq ft one-family home; after an about $371,000 loss, the policy was rescinded back to inception [The CoLiving Insider — RyLyOzBiWEs @ 00:02:42].

fields.name: safety_and_damage_waiver
fields.prompt: List the safety items that must be in place before any claim could ever be filed, and decide how guest damage is covered. Note smoke alarms, deadbolts, and window screens, plus the damage waiver amount and the coverage it buys.
fields.example: Working smoke alarms installed, dual cylinder deadbolts removed, and screens on all operable windows before any claim can be filed [Blue Fox Properties — 7sscnFcWkp4 @ 00:04:30]. Damage approach: a non-refundable $50 or $100 damage waiver backing about $500 of self-insured guest damage [Jacob and Elissa — ZoPbBZvfW94 @ 00:08:16]. Breakage responsibility spelled out in the lease up front.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when each lease has a priced exit in months of rent, state rules are confirmed, a termination agreement template is ready, the policy is rewritten as a dwelling fire DP3 with at least $500,000 liability, the use disclosure is sent in writing, and safety items are installed.
